svg.title: The 13 mutations of inter-universal Teichmüller theory — docs/IDENTIFIERS.md

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The 13 mutations of inter-universal Teichmüller theory

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: [IUTchIV] §3 calls a type of mathematical object a species and a functor between species a mutation; a mutation-history is an oriented graph with species at its vertices and mutations at its edges, and the log-theta-lattice is the mutation-history

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: that matters. The toolkit implements each of its 19 species as a C struct and each of these 13 mutations as a C function (iut_mutation_table in src/iut_ids.c, printed by iut species and docs/IDENTIFIERS.md). This page draws the graph they form,

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: what each one carries across — and what it forgets, rebuilds or only keeps up to an indeterminacy — and where each is defined, implemented and demonstrated.

svg.text: The mutation-history: 19 species as vertices, 13 mutations as edges

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: [IUTchIV] Def 3.3 (iii). Boxes are species (C structs), arrows are mutations (C functions), numbered as in the cards below. The three vertices {n,m}, {n+1,m}, {n,m+1} are the same species: the log-theta-lattice is this graph unrolled over Z², the log-link ① vertical

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: and one of the Θ×μ-links ②–④ horizontal. Green arrows are cores — observables all of whose mutations are isomorphisms, the data that survive a link — and lead to the coric species D⊢, (n,◦)HT^D, F⊢×μ and I(D⊢).

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The pattern is the theory: a Θ-type link keeps G_v ↷ O×μ and dilates the value groups but discards Π_v and the rings; the log-link keeps the bases and rebuilds the monoids; the cores

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: keep only what both kinds of link keep, and the multiradial algorithm reconstructs the Θ-pilot from exactly that intersection, at the price of Ind1–Ind3.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Identifier and notation, domain → codomain in the species table, the definition implemented, what is kept (●), kept up to an indeterminacy (◐), rebuilt (○) or forgotten (—), the C function behind it and the processes (iut run <id>) that demonstrate it on actual Θ-data.

svg.text: At every v the units O×_{†v} go through the p-adic logarithm to

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: log(O×), which becomes the additive module of a fresh copy ‡K_v

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: whose monoid O▷_{‡v} is then rebuilt. Π_v and G_v are identified (D

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: and D⊢ are vertically coric); the ring structures are not, and the

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Kummer isomorphisms of † and ‡ are not compatible with log (Prop 1.2

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: (iv)). The image of †O× rescaled by (p*)⁻¹ is the log-shell I_v ⊆ ‡K_v.
